newsitem.title: UK: British minority party promises "heaven on earth".
newsitem.headline: British minority party promises "heaven on earth".

text.p: The tiny Natural Law Party launched its manifesto on Friday and promised to create "heaven on earth" in Britain through collective meditation if it won the May 1 general election.
The party said some 300 candidates would contest seats under the banner: "The Natural Law Party -- Forming a proper government to create a happy, prosperous, problem-free nation."

Party leaders said they aimed to set up a group of 7,000 specialists in Transcendental Meditation (TM) and advanced Yogic Flying to unlock the latent brain power of Britain and save millions in government expenditure.
"The Natural Law Party is a blueprint to make heaven on earth in this country," deputy party leader Peter Warburton told a news conference to launch the manifesto.
He said feelings of "bubbling bliss" and "intense happiness" created by Yogic Flying would help Britons fulfil their potential and lead to a more efficient nation.
Yogic Flying and TM consist of repeating a word or a phrase -- known as a mantra -- to the point where devotees say they feel they can float.
"It leaves you feeling really good," said a party supporter who would not give her name. "In my experience, it's a jolly good thing."
Party leader Geoffrey Clements said the party would reduce the health service budget by 20 billion pounds ($32.6 billion) a year within three years by introducing natural medicine.

Other key policies include setting up an all-party government, banning the arms trade, introducing preventative medicine and meditation in schools as well as fighting crime by using meditation to reduce stress.
The party was founded in 1992 in response to what its leaders saw as widespread dissatisfaction with existing parties.
"It's very clear that nothing new is being offered by the old parties," Clements said. "A vote for old parties is a vote for conflict and a vote for failure."
The party said it had fielded 310 candidates in the 1992 election and won an average of 0.4 percent of the vote in the constituencies it contested.
The party's meditation techniques were handed down by Maharishi Mahesh Yogi, an Indian mystic who converted the Beatles to TM during the 1960s. He believes there is infinite intelligence in nature.
